authors.bio: Alan Lambshead is vice president of engineering, at Evertz Microsystems Ltd. in Burlington, Ontario, Canada where his responsibilities include the general oversight of R & D and product development, focusing on time code and post-production products. During his 30 years at Evertz, Lambshead has been an active member on SMPTE Technology committees and is the author of several SMPTE recommended practices. He is a member of the Toronto Section of SMPTE and has presented papers at local chapter and national conferences of SMPTE. Lambshead is a widely recognized expert in the field of HDTV time code and sync issues, HDTV production, HDTV metadata, and film-to-video transfers. Lambshead graduated from McMaster University, Hamilton Ontario with a B. Eng in electrical engineering in 1972 and became licensed as a Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) in Ontario in 1988. He became a Fellow of the Society in 2009.
authors.name: Alan Lambshead

authors.bio: John Footen has been in the media technology business for more than 25 years. His career has focused on leading-edge product development and integration. He has led numerous projects for broadcasters, studios and other media companies around the world. He is degreed in film and television production, as well as computer science from New York University. He was most recently a vice president at National TeleConsultants, and is now chief technology officer at Chime Media. Footen is a regular speaker at conferences such as SMPTE, NAB, IBC, and Digital Hollywood. He is member of the Board of Directors for the Advanced Media Workflow Association, chairs the Media Services Architecture Group, and co-chairs the joint FIMS initiative with the EBU. He is co-chair of 32NF in SMPTE. He is an inventor on several media-related patents and has led teams whose work has received technical Emmy awards. Footen is author of articles for publications such as the SMPTE Journal and Broadcast Engineering. He is a columnist for TV Technology and the co-author of a book about the application of SOA, BPM and Web Services in media, “The Service-Oriented Media Enterprise” with Joey Faust.
authors.name: John Footen
